title: Adjacent cohomology compatibility for finite quotient h-maps
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, $y\in Y$ and $p\in\mathbb N$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_A$, $X'=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\times_Y X$, $g:X'\to X$, $F'=g^*F$, $J=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_{X'}$, $X_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^{n+1})\times_Y X$, $i_n:X_n\to X$, $j_n:X_n\to X'$ and $F_n=i_n^*F$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback, def-nagata-extended-ideal, def-weil-pbc-formal-fibre-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-formal-functions-finite-pullback]. Let $S_n=H^p(X',F'/J^{n+1}F')$ with its $A$-action, and let $T_n=H^p(X_n,F_n)$ with its $A$-action obtained by restricting the completed-ring action. Give $S$ its quotient transitions $s_n:S_{n+1}\to S_n$ and $T$ its fibre-cohomology transitions $t_n:T_{n+1}\to T_n$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, def-weil-pbc-formal-fibre-cohomology]. Suppose maps $e_n:F'/J^{n+1}F'\to j_{n,*}F_n$ satisfy $e_n\circ q_n=u_n$, where $q_n$ is the quotient projection and $u_n$ is formalFunctionsFiniteFMap. Then for every $n\ge0$ and $x\in S_{n+1}$, $H(j_n,e_n)(s_n(x))=t_n(H(j_{n+1},e_{n+1})(x))$, where $H(j,e)$ is moduleCohomologyFMap. The $e_n$ need not be invertible.

source.place: Tags 02OD, 01F7 and 01FB; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02OD and the individual cited tags

proof.text: Let t_n : X_n -> X_(n+1) be the infinitesimal transition. Pullback uniqueness identifies t_n followed by j_(n+1) with j_n. Apply the Hom equivalences defining the finite and transition FMaps: their unit equations imply that composing these h-maps gives the finite unit at level n, after the canonical pushforward-composition congruence.

For arbitrary e_n factoring the finite units, precompose the sheaf transition square with q_(n+1). The defining cokernel equation for the quotient transition and the preceding unit identity make its two sides equal. Cancel this epi sheaf quotient projection. Do not cancel the induced map on cohomology, which need not be epi.

Apply source naturality and composition of moduleCohomologyFMap to the sheaf square. The canonical pushforward congruence transports the map for t_n followed by j_(n+1) to the map for j_n. Forget scalar restrictions, which leave the additive maps unchanged. The adjacent maps of formalCompletionSystem and formalFibreCohomologySystem are respectively the quotient transition and the cohomology transition. This proves the displayed identity for every p and n.

proof_origin.place: Tags 02OD, 01F7 and 01FB; canonical-map and adjunction details expanded from these proofs

mathlib_searches.query: Cohomology of an ideal quotient sheaf equals cohomology on its closed subscheme, compatibly with infinitesimal transitions
A closed immersion gives a quotient sheaf isomorphism compatible with adjunction units and cohomology transitions
